note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank ranking was read): Al Rajhi Bank, the Saudi National Bank and Riyad Bank. The Saudi National Bank's sites (alahli.com, snb.com.sa) didn't answer this research's connections on 2026-10-30 and weren't read; Bank AlJazira's card, read on 2026-10-29, is kept. All these cards are Islamic: the bank charges a monthly profit margin on what's carried instead of interest, written as a monthly rate. Al Rajhi Bank's credit card terms and conditions (the May 2026 edition linked from its card pages), read in full: the issuance or annual fee for the primary card (Platinum 490, Signature 790, Infinite 990, Selective 790 riyals), a monthly profit rate of 2.5%, a foreign transaction fee of 2%, a cash withdrawal or transfer fee of 3% for amounts below 2,500 riyals and at most 75 riyals at or above it (written as 3% with a ceiling of 75; free for the first 100 days, not written), and a minimum payment of 5% or 100 riyals, whichever is higher; its fees don't include VAT, which its own example charges at 15% on the foreign transaction fee, written as a 15% tax on fees. The Marriott Bonvoy card's page gives its annual fee, 1,200 riyals (1,380 with VAT in its example), and the same profit rate, minimum, foreign and cash fees. The Platinum card's page waives its issuance and annual fees for cards issued from 1 October to 31 December 2026, a campaign that isn't written. The terms state a grace period of at least 25 days from the statement to pay, not the days a purchase goes without profit, which isn't written; they state no late fee. Riyad Bank's Islamic credit card fees table (in its Islamic credit card application form, linked from its card pages; undated, its APRs following the central bank's rules of 8 November 2022), read in full: each of its eleven Islamic cards' annual fee, collected after the card is activated, its monthly profit margin, its additional fee on international transactions (2%, 1.90% on the Mastercard World Elite), a cash withdrawal fee of 3% below 2,500 riyals with at most 75 at or above it, and a late payment fee of 50 riyals. The Titanium card's own page gives its fee (290) and its monthly term cost (2.55%); the card pages give the minimum payment, 5% of the total due or 100 riyals (200 on the Mastercard World and World Elite). The World Elite's fee waived for private banking customers and the World's for Diamond banking customers aren't written, the game holding no such tier. The Dufaat Plus card, repaid in instalments with no annual fee or profit rate, isn't written: its balance isn't carried the way a card's is. Supplementary card, replacement, change of partner, reactivation, dispute and credit shield fees aren't written: a holder meets them only by asking. Bank AlJazira's initial disclosure for its credit cards: the Visa Classic's annual fee is 150 riyals, subject to VAT, which the form's own examples charge at 15% (172.50 in all), and its monthly profit margin is 2.20% (26.4% a year). Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: Bank AlJazira's initial disclosure, read again, gives the minimum monthly payment, 5% of the outstanding balance or 200 riyals, whichever is higher, written on the Visa Classic.
